record.original_question: Given a graph embedded on a surface, is there a polynomial-time algorithm to find a shortest contractible cycle, a shortest surface-separating cycle, and a shortest orientation-preserving cycle?

evidence.quote: Question 9.3 Let G be embedded on a surface. Do there exist polynomial-time algorithms to find: • a shortest contractible cycle in G? • a shortest surface-separating cycle in G? • a shortest orientation-preserving cycle in G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite graph cellularly embedded in a (possibly non-orientable) closed surface Σ, with positive edge weights. A cycle in G is a closed walk visiting each vertex at most once; viewed as a closed curve on Σ, it is called:
(a) contractible, if it is null-homotopic in Σ;
(b) surface-separating, if removing its image disconnects Σ;
(c) orientation-preserving (two-sided), if a small tubular neighborhood of it in Σ is an annulus (rather than a Möbius band).
Determine whether each of the following three problems admits a polynomial-time algorithm in the size of G:
1. Compute a shortest contractible cycle in G.
2. Compute a shortest surface-separating cycle in G.
3. Compute a shortest orientation-preserving cycle in G.
artifact.status_search_result: All three subquestions appear to be resolved. Cabello (SODA 2008 / "Finding shortest contractible and shortest separating cycles in embedded graphs") gave a polynomial-time algorithm for a shortest contractible cycle and proved that finding a shortest surface-separating cycle is NP-hard. For shortest orientation-preserving (Π-two-sided) cycles, a polynomial-time algorithm is known (e.g., the work on "Finding short cycles in an embedded graph in polynomial time", arXiv:0807.1620, which resolved the corresponding open problem of Mohar–Thomassen).

status_evidence.title: Finding shortest contractible and shortest separating cycles in embedded graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm for a shortest contractible cycle; finding a shortest separating cycle in an embedded graph is NP-hard.

status_evidence.title: Finding Short Cycles in an Embedded Graph in Polynomial Time (arXiv:0807.1620)
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomially bounded algorithm to find a shortest Π-two-sided (orientation-preserving) cycle in an embedded graph, resolving an open problem of Mohar and Thomassen.
status_evidence.claim: Shortest orientation-preserving cycle can be computed in polynomial time.
